plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x4 time course
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question — which genes change in a treatment-specific way across t0..t3, beyond the shared time trend — is exactly a condition:time interaction test on a bulk RNA-seq count matrix. The data are 12,000 genes x 24 samples (counts.csv has 25 columns: a gene-id column plus 24 sample columns), with metadata.csv giving condition, time (t0..t3) and time_hours for each of the 24 samples: 2 conditions x 4 time points x 3 replicates. That is 24 samples for a full interaction model with 8 coefficient groups, i.e. 16 residual df — enough for DESeq2's LRT but not for anything more elaborate; every step must state that power limit rather than paper over it.

T1S1 builds the DESeq2 object and does QC: it must first resolve the ambiguity flagged in the data profile (the counts are salmon gene-level output and the record does not state whether length correction was already applied), by checking whether the values are integers; non-integers mean the matrix carries length-scaled/abundance-derived values and must be rounded with that caveat recorded, since DESeq2 requires counts. It then checks library sizes, filters low-count genes, runs VST, and inspects PCA/sample distances for whether time and condition separate as designed and whether any replicate is an outlier. T1S2 is the primary test: a DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test of the full model ~condition + time + condition:time against the reduced ~condition + time, which by construction removes the shared time trend and the constant treatment offset and leaves only genes whose trajectory shape differs between conditions. Because time has only four discrete levels, treating time as a factor is preferred over a continuous or spline term — it makes no shape assumption and the 4 levels cost only 3 extra df. T1S3 resolves where in time the interaction acts, via the per-time-point condition contrasts (t1, t2, t3 each relative to the shared intercept structure) and their differences from t0, so a gene called significant by the LRT can be described as early, late, or sustained. T1S4 clusters the significant genes' condition-difference trajectories to give a small set of interpretable response shapes.

T2S1 (parallel, depends only on T1S2/T1S3 output) runs pathway enrichment on the interaction gene set against human hallmark and GO BP sets, which the reference store holds for Homo sapiens; if the counts carry Ensembl IDs rather than symbols, the step maps them via the staged human UniProt ID mapping or org.Hs.eg.db. Enrichment is an annotation layer — if the gene sets are absent the step reports that and the interaction result stands on its own.

A sensitivity check is folded into T1S2 rather than made a separate track: refitting the LRT with time_hours as a continuous linear term shows how much of the interaction signal is a simple divergence in slope versus a non-monotonic shape, and disagreement between the two parameterizations is reported rather than hidden.
